## TDD evidence

- [ ] I implemented the minimum change required to make it pass.
- [ ] I refactored only while the suite remained green.
- [ ] Tests assert behaviour/invariants rather than merely increasing coverage.

## Verification

- [ ] Relevant tests pass deterministically.
- [ ] Full test suite passes.
- [ ] Coverage gate passes with no unexplained reduction.
- [ ] No retry was added to hide flaky behaviour.

<!-- Also run before every push: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`,

## Versioning

<!-- CONTRIBUTING.md "Versioning": can taking this upgrade turn a green build red
without me changing anything? Tick exactly one. A bump dates its CHANGELOG.md entry
under that version and leaves no [Unreleased] section; merging the bump is the
release. The `gate` check fails a change to `src/`, `schemas/`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`
or a published `package.json` field without the bump. -->

- [ ] **patch** — closes a bypass at the same severity, fixes a false positive, or docs that ship
- [ ] **minor** — new surface (a `warn` rule, an adapter, a command or flag, a gated graduation)
- [ ] **major** — turns green builds red uninvited (a new `block` rule, `warn` → `block` for v1 policies, a breaking CLI, exit-code, hook or schema change)
- [ ] **no bump** — nothing shipped changes (tests, CI, community-health files, docs outside the published surface)

## DDD / architecture

- [ ] Domain language is consistent.
- [ ] Domain code does not depend directly on infrastructure frameworks.
- [ ] Invariants are enforced in the domain model where appropriate.
- [ ] Any dependency-boundary change is explained below.
- [ ] The design follows the repository's architecture standard or documents why it intentionally differs.
- [ ] A consequential architectural decision has an ADR, or no ADR is required.

## Security and trust

<!-- What this changes about what the gate allows, denies or trusts. A detector change
ships evasion tests and at least one negative that must not fire; a fixed bypass is now a
permanent regression test. A counted-round record (PREDICTION*, DEVIATIONS, ROUND*-*)
reaches main only through a maintainer-merged PR. -->

## Scope

- [ ] This PR has one clear purpose.
- [ ] Unrelated refactors and formatting changes are excluded.
- [ ] Follow-up work is split into separate issues/PRs.

## Self-explanatory code

- [ ] Production and test code contains no explanatory comments.
- [ ] Intent is expressed through names, types, structure, and tests.
